headline: Wrexham's 4-1 win, 7 players out — and a level game
summary: Wrexham arrive at Ewood Park after a 4-1 home win over Preston, creating 1.97 expected goals to 0.79. But Phil Parkinson travels with 7 players out, Max Cleworth and Nathan Broadhead among them — 'probably the worst spell' of his time there, he said. Blackburn led at West Brom on Saturday and lost 3-2, and they concede 2.0 expected goals a game. Even so, Wrexham are narrow favourites at 36%, with Blackburn close behind at 34.5% — the two sides rated level. Over 2.25 goals is close to even, at 50.4%.
read: Wrexham are the narrow favourites at Ewood Park, but the handicap line is level: one point and four places separate two mid-table sides, and neither has pulled away. Blackburn create little and concede plenty, Wrexham are down to seven absentees, so the goals line sits at two and a half with the over a coin-flip.

facts.fact: Wrexham are the narrow favourites for Ewood Park, with a 36.0% fair chance of the away win against Blackburn's 34.5%.
facts.meaning: Nothing separates the sides — neither team is a clear favourite, and a draw is a live result at 29.5%.

facts.meaning: Their sharpest attacking display of the run, and it came at the end of a week of noise around the manager.

facts.fact: Blackburn led 2-0 at West Brom on 17 October and lost 3-2.
facts.meaning: They score, they lead, and they still lose — a shape that keeps opponents alive in games Blackburn should be drawing.

facts.fact: Wrexham have seven players sidelined, with Max Cleworth, Nathan Broadhead and Sheaf among them — a situation Phil Parkinson called 'probably the worst spell in his time here'.
facts.meaning: Wrexham travel with a patched-up squad and a reshuffled XI at Ewood Park.

facts.fact: Blackburn have conceded 2.0 xG per game across their last five matches while creating 1.05.
facts.meaning: They give up more and better chances than they make — every Blackburn game stays open longer than it should.

facts.meaning: Neither side gets a head start; the level result the market sees is a draw.

facts.fact: Over 2.25 goals is priced at 50.4% — a genuine coin-flip on three goals or more.

facts.meaning: The absentee closest to a return — a boost for a squad down to bare bones in midfield.

sources.fact: Blackburn surrendered a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 at West Bromwich Albion in their most recent Championship match.
BBC Radio Lancashire's Andy Bayes says Blackburn's loss to West Brom is far from a disaster and there is much to be pleased about despite blowing a 2-0 lead.
Blackburn's new away ticket policy, designed to reward supporters who spend the most, has been criticised as a slippery slope for travelling fans.
Wrexham returned to winning ways with an impressive 4-1 victory over Preston North End last weekend.

Phil Parkinson said Wrexham had to block outside noise and called the club's injury situation unprecedented, probably the worst spell in his time there, with Max Cleworth, Nathan Broadhead and Dan Sheaf among those sidelined.
The Athletic reports that Phil Parkinson's future had been under close scrutiny but the win over Preston brought him some welcome breathing space.
Ben Sheaf is set to return to full training and could be available for Wrexham against Blackburn at Ewood Park on Saturday.
Wrexham currently have seven players sidelined with injuries, and Phil Parkinson faces more selection decisions ahead of the trip to Blackburn.
